questions.subject: BUSINESS_ENTREPRENEURSHIP
questions.stem: Umberwood reported a profit from home cleaning services sales but still ran short of cash that month. Which explanation is most plausible?

options.text: The firm sold products only for immediate cash
options.misconception: Would improve cash rather than deplete it

options.text: Profit and cash flow are identical accounting measures
options.misconception: Denies the timing difference between them

options.text: Customers were given credit terms and had not yet paid
The company earned revenue but had no expenses
options.misconception: Would increase cash, not create a shortage

questions.explanation: Accrual profit is recorded when revenue is earned, not when cash arrives. If customers buy on credit, sales appear in profit before payment, so a profitable firm can still face a cash shortage while receivables are outstanding.
questions.hint: Think about the timing of revenue versus cash collection.

questions.subject: BUSINESS_ENTREPRENEURSHIP
questions.stem: Umberleaf has average accounts receivable of $250,000 and credit sales of $50,000 per month. Approximately how many days of sales are tied up in receivables?
questions.explanation: Days sales outstanding is average receivables divided by daily credit sales. Monthly sales of $50,000 imply daily sales near $1,667, so $250,000 divided by that daily figure is roughly 150 days.
questions.hint: Convert monthly sales to daily, then divide receivables by it.
